figures.alt: Shower waterproofing stage with sloped pan, curb, membrane, and plumbing rough-in
figures.caption: The waterproofing stage is one of the points where a bath timeline cannot be rushed. The pan, curb, drain, wall transitions, and inspection sequence must be right before tile hides the work.

figures.alt: Vanity cabinet with accessible sink P-trap and supply valves
figures.caption: Coordinate vanity dimensions and plumbing access before countertop and finish work. A beautiful cabinet is still a poor installation if shutoffs and drains cannot be serviced.

figures.alt: Shower valve access point prepared for service behind finished wall material
figures.caption: Plan serviceability with the finished wall assembly in mind. Valve, trim, and access details should be confirmed before the final closeout phase.
